comments.text: the house part's entry, where the street part's loader jumps after loading MAIN: JMP $13FE, which sets the house up and falls into the main loop
the first of four hooks the resident disk code calls to show its messages: select text window A (JMP $6817)
hook: wait for a key or the joystick (JMP $6303)
hook: clear the current text window (JMP $6A3E)
hook: print the text at X/Y (high/low) in the current window (JMP $6A83)
a 20-byte scratch line for text built at run time: the drive's status, the clock digits of "IT'S NOW n O'CLOCK", numbers for the panel
a byte the window printer keeps beside the text buffer (read at $6A16)
the end of the scratch line, $FF bytes

the house's table of files for the resident loader, five bytes each: name pointer, load address, disk side (0 for side 1, 1 for side 2). 0 ALTCH.CHA to $A000, 1 SCREEN to $9800, 2 VENDING.SRT to $9000, 3 SCn.DAT (the level's objects) to $8000, 4 Dn (the level's map) to $B000, 5 Dn.CUR (the level's saved state) to $9800, 6 ARTn.ICN to $A000, 7 INIT (the street part) to $1390 on side 1, 8 SAVE.DAT to $9C00, 9 Dn to $A000, 10 DEATH to $9080, 11 COPY to $9800, 12 MSG to $9800, 13 HOUSE to $8000, 14 SONG to $B000. The digits in the level files' names are patched in for the level being entered
JSR $15EA to set the house up, then the main loop

the house's main loop, one pass per round of play: the clock ($1495), Freddy's attacks on the friends ($152B), the player ($234B), the monsters ($494A), shots and powers ($2590), the haunted items ($1439), object animation ($4D0D), the panel ($37BD) and the message timer ($1EF3), until the game-over flag $79C4 is set
game over or a new game: sets $0C4F to 1, pushes $138F as a return address and has the resident loader load file 7, INIT, so that its RTS lands on the street part's entry at $1390

unless the player carries FREDDY'S GLOVE (item $45), a carried LANTERN ($43) or FREDDY'S HAT ($44) counts down its own timer ($79FA, $79F7) once a pass; at zero the timer is reset to 16, the message reads "<item> IS ATTACKING YOU!" and a monster is sent at the player ($440E)
" IS ATTACKING YOU!" (CR, $00 ended), printed after the item's name

the clock: subtracts 23 from a fraction byte each pass; on each wrap it counts down the attack timer $79E4, and on level 10 (unless the final fight has started) it counts 120 wraps to an hour, prints "IT'S NOW n O'CLOCK" and calls $5BD2; at 12 o'clock it calls $60EC (turns the level's monsters loose) and sets $73B3
"IT'S NOW " and " O'CLOCK" (CR, $00 ended), around the hour digits in the text buffer

when the attack timer $79E4 runs out it is reset to 240 and Freddy picks a random friend who is neither the player nor rescued: that friend loses a point of soul ($7368, and status 2, dead, at 0), the panel box is redrawn, message 35 and the friend's name are shown with sound 23; if the friend is on the player's level a monster of kind 5 is placed at the friend's spot ($17C7), and a friend who has just died is replaced by object $16 on the map

sets the house up after the load: pointers and the random seed ($164E), the party ($1843), the attack timer, message 1 ("TIME PASSES..."), sound 34, the level's files unless a saved game is being loaded ($572F), the sprites ($16A6), the colours and the panel

copies a block of memory, described by the six bytes after the JSR: source (2 bytes), destination (2 bytes), length (2 bytes); returns past them. Used to keep the screen, colour RAM and character set aside at $9000-$9FFF while a picture or menu covers them, and to bring them back
sets the screen ($CC00) and colour RAM ($D800) pointers the drawing routines use and the text colour, seeds the random generator from the jiffy clock, and empties the keyboard buffer
code nothing calls in the house: switches the video chip to the bank at $C000 through CIA 2, turns the screen's bitmap mode off and the sprites off
the player's sprites: colours (sprite 0 black, the rest white, shared colours 6 and 2), positions 120,125 for sprites 0 and 1, no expansion, sprite 1 multicolour, sprites 0 and 1 on
sets sprite A's X position to Y with bit 8 from X (in $D010)
sets sprite A's Y position to Y
clears the 24 animation counters at $7650, copies every eighth byte of the table at $7578 into $7668, then calls $386C, $384A, $388C and $38AA
clears the eight monster slots, marks each free (kind 6), finds the level's monster list from its number, and places up to six monsters from it at their map spots ($17C7)

puts a monster of kind A at the map cell $79CC,$79CD in slot X, unless the player stands within two cells of it: three of its properties come from the kind tables at $743E, $7482 and $746D, and its picture from $7458; kind 5 takes it from a table indexed by the level instead

starts a game from what the street part handed over: the sound switch ($0C4C), a saved game to load ($0C4D, which goes to $4398), the panel mode ($0C4E) and the character the player chose ($0C4F); the four friends who are not the player are each given one of ten hiding places at random (level, X, Y from $190E, $1918 and $1922), the inventory is emptied ($4D in every slot but the first), and the player starts at the level's entrance
a flag for each of the ten hiding places, cleared as each is handed out so that no two friends share one
the level of each of the ten hiding places
the map column of each hiding place
the map row of each hiding place
draws character X's box in the panel: the name, then "LEVEL n" (the level the friend is held on, or the player's own level), "RESCUED" or "R.I.P.", and the SOUL bar, with the POWR bar for the player
the panel's words: "LEVEL nn", "RESCUED ", "R.I.P.  ", "SOUL", "POWR"
copies a panel word (up to its $00, as screen codes) to the screen at ($61) and colours it white at ($FB)

draws a 3 by 3 character picture of object A (an item, a monster or a map feature) on the screen at column X, row Y, from the 9 character codes and 9 colours at $A800 + A times 18; an animated object ($4E-$65) takes its current frame from $7650 first
copies the 8 bytes of character X of the panel set at $A000 into character Y of the play-area set at $D000, with the I/O switched out for the copy

redraws the 21 rows of the play area from the off-screen copy at $98A7 and $9CA7 (characters and colours, 33 wide), waiting for the raster to be between lines $78 and $88 first so the redraw does not tear; while $79D5 is set, each cell is first tested by $3D5B and a cell it rejects is blanked
$FB-$FC = the address in the level map at $B000 of the cell at column $79CC, row $79CD (64 cells to a row)

puts up the rest of a full-screen picture whose character set the last inline copy moved: a picture file (.SRT) is 2 KB of characters, 1000 screen codes and 1000 colours, so this copies the 1000 bytes at the copy's source plus $0800 to the screen at $CC00 and the next 1000 to colour RAM at $D800, through two inline copies whose sources it patches
